alignments.note: The fixed expression sons of foreignness is rendered by the single lexical substantive foreigners; the supplied article joins it.
The reflexive themselves renders the Hebrew verb's voice.
The temporal preposition is expanded as the subordinate relation As soon as; the closing as carries the relation.

Hearing of an ear is jointly recast as they hear: the infinitive carries the auditory predicate and its supplied subject, while ear specifies the hearing within the same rendering. Retain the two-morpheme expression rather than treating ear as omitted; the ASV writes no independent word for that specification. The temporal preposition separately owns As soon as.

The ASV supplies of me as the content heard; no object or possessive morpheme in the hearing phrase licenses it. The verse's two first-person suffixes already realize the separate complements of submit and obey. Unlike the infinitive's supplied subject, this complement is not part of its grammatical rendering.
The bare-object recasting leaves the preposition unexpressed.

review_notes: The ASV margin offers yield feigned obedience and notes the literal Hebrew lie; the alignment follows submit themselves.
